passage:
I thought I was being kind. When we married, I took all the money matters: the loans, the savings, the bills, the tax forms. It was easier that way, I told myself, and Rajni never asked. Then in March a big repair bill for our flat's roof arrived after the rains. Rajni asked where we stood, and I said, "Don't worry about it." She said, "I don't know what we owe or what we have." She wasn't angry so much as hurt. Looking back, keeping everything to myself wasn't ease. It was a kind of control I'd never named. It took us months of small, awkward talks to rebuild trust.

Hemant

qa.a: Hemant could have shown Rajni the accounts and the loans and shared the tasks, because knowing the full picture lets both handle a sudden expense together.

qa.a: Rajni probably felt hurt and left out, not knowing what the couple owed or had.

Family counsellor's note — Abhinav and Shalmali, second session. Written by Francis.

At the first session Shalmali described the evening that brought them here. Her father had been admitted to hospital, and she asked Abhinav what they could use from their savings. He paused and then told her that most of it was tied up in a car loan and a fixed deposit she had never heard of.
Abhinav explained, calmly, that he had handled all their money since the wedding "to keep things simple". He had not thought to discuss the loan.
Shalmali said the hospital bill wasn't what hurt most. "I didn't know my own life." She said she now checks his phone when he isn't looking, and hates that she does.
Abhinav looked shaken to hear this.
What I did next: I asked them to bring every account statement next week and go through it together, with me present.

qa.q: What was Shalmali's father admitted to?
What did Shalmali mean by "I didn't know my own life"?
qa.a: She felt shut out and betrayed, since important decisions about their shared money had been made without her.

qa.q: What else could Abhinav have done from the start of the marriage?
qa.a: He could have shared all accounts and loans and made money decisions together, even if he still handled the paperwork.

qa.q: How is Abhinav affected by hearing Shalmali's feelings?
qa.a: Abhinav looks shaken, realising that what he thought was keeping things simple has cost her trust.

grounding: It shows a husband handling all money without discussion, so his wife doesn't know the loans and savings and a sudden expense causes tension and mistrust.

Wednesday night

The garage said the scooter repair would be big, and I thought, fine, we'll use the savings. Samir went quiet, then said there wasn't much in the savings right now.
"What do you mean?"
"I lent some to my cousin. And there's the personal loan for the wedding."
A loan. For our wedding. That I never knew about.
He said he didn't tell me because he "handles money" and didn't want me to worry. Since the wedding he's done everything: the bank, the bills, the passwords. I thought that was sweet. I never asked. That's partly on me.
But tonight I looked at him and felt like I didn't know him. Not because of the money. Because of the silence.
We slept back to back. Tomorrow I'm asking to see every statement, together.
— Ritu

qa.q: How might Samir feel lying back to back that night?
qa.a: Samir is likely guilty and anxious, realising that keeping money matters to himself has damaged Ritu's trust.
